text: I follow the public road to the gate of Ashbridge. If someone is on duty, I ask where a newcomer could lend a hand today.
intent_before_narration: Proceed only from the verge to the gate. Ask for a lead; no agreement to go elsewhere or take a job.

text: I step clear of the cart. Before I go in, which way is the Weary Ox, and is Marta a fair person to work for?
intent_before_narration: Step aside within gate area and ask directions/opinion; no departure for tavern yet.

text: I thank them, go in and follow the cooper's-yard directions to the Weary Ox. At the door I ask for Marta.
intent_before_narration: Travel to the specified tavern by the described route and ask for Marta. No employment, purchase or onward trip.

text: Alaric. The watch said you sometimes need a hand. I can do a short errand or help someone get where they're going; what's needed this morning?
intent_before_narration: Make a work inquiry at the doorway; hear terms. No agreement or movement yet.

text: Yes, it's a deal. I shoulder the herring keg and take it to Bren's stall on the west side of the market. What word does he want carried back?
intent_before_narration: Accept Marta's specific errand and carry her keg to Bren at his market stall; offer delivery and request reply. Do not return or collect wages yet.

text: I'll pass it on. I take the dill back to Marta at the Weary Ox. 'Good and whole,' I tell her, and hand her the dill. 'Bren sends his compliments to the cook, if not to the brewer.'
intent_before_narration: Return to Marta at the Ox and deliver the message and dill; legitimate agreed wages may be offered. No new errand accepted.

text: Thanks, Marta. I'll leave the afternoon hauling for another day. Over the bread and cheese I ask Hal about Otty. Is he going out to check on that broken stall? I could give them a hand.
intent_before_narration: Decline the afternoon job; eat offered meal and ask Hal about Otty and whether he is going. No permission yet to follow Hal or leave.

text: I thank Marta for the boards. Once I have eaten, I shoulder a couple from the woodpile and head to the drain corner to find Otty. I would like to hear what she wants done with her table.
intent_before_narration: Accept the errand, carry boards to Otty, and consult her before repairing the table.

text: I can drive a straight nail most days. I take her hammer and fit the boards where she showed me, picking the honest nails out of the pot. When the top sits level, I give it a gentle push to see if it rocks.
intent_before_narration: Rebuild the stall under Otty's direction and check its stability.

text: I lift the nail-pot onto the new top and sit with her for a minute. Keep the kindling for someone with a hearth, Otty. I spend a fair bit of my time on the road. What is there to see on foot just outside Ashbridge?
intent_before_narration: Decline the kindling, chat with Otty, and ask for a nearby walking destination. I haven't chosen a destination yet.

text: Today I can walk for the pleasure of my legs. The herons sound worth the mud. I wish her a good day's trade and walk out by the west gate, taking the river path as far as the water meadows.
intent_before_narration: Head to the water meadows for a walk and watch for herons. The mill is an option for later.

text: One copper for me, then. I put it in the thin man's hand and, if he lets me by, follow the bank to the dead willow. I sit quietly there to watch the shallows.
intent_before_narration: Pay the one copper requested for passage and continue to the willow to look for herons.

text: I watch until one of the herons fishes, or until my legs start to go to sleep. Then I stretch them on the path up to Weirbridge mill. Otty put me in the mood to see Ashbridge from that rise.
intent_before_narration: Watch the herons for a little while, then walk on to the mill rise for the view.

text: I would like some company for the way back. In the mill yard I hail whoever is minding the sacks. Has anyone a load going down to Ashbridge who would like a hand with the lifting?
intent_before_narration: Ask in the yard about accompanying a wagon to Ashbridge in exchange for help loading. Find out whether anyone is going.

text: I'll wait here for Tam and take my share of the hauling down to Ashbridge. There's time for a breather first. I find a patch of shade in the yard and hold out a hand for the dog to sniff if he likes.
intent_before_narration: Agree to accompany Tam and help with the cart at loading time. Rest in the mill yard until then.

text: I stay at Tam's side with a hand on the rail. Quietly, to the miller: This is your usual road. Do these two collect for anyone, or do you normally just tell them to let the cart through?
intent_before_narration: Stand by Tam and consult the miller about the demand. Let him explain how he wants to handle his cart.

text: Let this one be my expense, miller. I give the thin toll man two coppers for the whole cart and company. Once he has cleared the road, I help push the load with Tam to the west gate.
intent_before_narration: Pay the thin man the two coppers requested for everyone and get the cart and Tam to the west gate together.

text: The miller paid them himself. I tuck my coins away. I'll see the load home with you, Tam. I wheel the cart along with them to the storehouse by the market and ask the storekeeper where the sacks belong.
intent_before_narration: Leave the toll settled by the miller. Accompany Tam and the miller to the market storehouse and find the unloading spot.

text: Just the lifting today, Garl. I pass sacks down for the count and help Tam settle the last ones on the left of the post. When we're finished I thank the miller and his nephew for the company.
intent_before_narration: Decline further employment, help unload the whole cart as agreed, and say farewell.

text: I head back to the Weary Ox for the evening. If Marta has a minute, I tell her Otty put the boards to good use and that there were two herons out by the willow. Then I find a seat where I can put my feet up.
intent_before_narration: Return to the inn, share the outcome of the morning's favor with Marta, and rest for the evening.
